decisions.choice: his people, and he your God: the heart of the covenant
decisions.reason: These words are the covenant formula, the short summary of the bond between God and Israel: they belong to him, and he is their God (26:17-18; Exodus 6:7; Leviticus 26:12). Today in Moab that bond is confirmed for the generation about to enter the land.

decisions.choice: establish: set up, confirm
decisions.reason: The verb means to raise up or make stand, and so to confirm something already promised (8:18; 28:9). God made Israel his people at Sinai; here he confirms them as his people again.

decisions.choice: as he swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham to be God to him and to his descendants after him (Genesis 17:7-8), and he repeated the promise to Isaac and to Jacob (Genesis 26:3-4; 28:13-15). The covenant in Moab keeps that promise.

decisions.choice: as he spoke to you: what God has said to Israel itself
decisions.reason: Besides the oath to the ancestors, God has spoken this promise to Israel directly, at Sinai and through Moses (26:18; Exodus 19:5-6).

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ancestors" for "fathers", the forefathers of the nation named in the verse. Literal keeps "fathers".

decisions.choice: He wants to make you his own people
decisions.reason: Readable begins a new sentence, makes God the subject, and says "wants to" for the Hebrew "in order to", which states God's purpose in the covenant.

source.text: וְלֹ֥א אִתְּכֶ֖ם לְבַדְּכֶ֑ם אָנֹכִ֗י כֹּרֵת֙ אֶת־הַבְּרִ֣ית הַזֹּ֔את וְאֶת־הָאָלָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: And not with you by yourselves I [am] cutting the covenant the this and the oath the this,

en.L: And not with you alone am I making this covenant and this oath,
en.B: It is not with you alone that I am making this covenant and this oath,
en.R: I am not making this covenant and its oath only with you who are here.

es.L: Y no solo con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} hago yo este pacto y este juramento,
es.B: No es solo con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} con quienes hago este pacto y este juramento,
es.R: No hago este pacto y su juramento solo con {{plural_you:ustedes, los que están aquí|vosotros, los que estáis aquí}}.

fr.L: Et ce n’est pas avec vous seuls que je conclus cette alliance et ce serment,
fr.B: Ce n’est pas seulement avec vous que je conclus cette alliance et ce serment,
fr.R: Je ne conclus pas cette alliance et son serment seulement avec vous qui êtes ici.

sw.L: Wala si pamoja nanyi peke yenu ninalifanya agano hili na kiapo hiki,
sw.B: Sifanyi agano hili na kiapo hiki pamoja nanyi peke yenu,
sw.R: Sifanyi agano hili na kiapo chake pamoja nanyi tu mlio hapa.

decisions.choice: I am making: Moses speaks as the one who makes the covenant on the LORD's behalf
decisions.reason: In verse 11 it is the LORD who makes the covenant; here Moses says "I", and in verse 14 he says "the LORD our God", so the speaker is Moses. He acts as the LORD's go-between, setting out the covenant and calling the people into it, as at Horeb (5:5).

decisions.choice: not with you alone: the sentence runs on into verse 14
decisions.reason: The verse sets up a contrast that verse 14 completes: not with you alone, but also with those who are not here today.

decisions.choice: this oath: the sworn pledge of the covenant
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, the oath is the solemn pledge that binds the covenant and calls down its curses on those who break it.

decisions.choice: only with you who are here
decisions.reason: Readable adds "who are here" to prepare for verse 14, which names those who are not here.

source.text: כִּי֩ אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֶשְׁנ֜וֹ פֹּ֗ה עִמָּ֨נוּ֙ עֹמֵ֣ד הַיּ֔וֹם לִפְנֵ֖י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וְאֵ֨ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵינֶ֛נּוּ פֹּ֖ה עִמָּ֥נוּ הַיּֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: but with whoever is here with us standing the day before Yahweh our God, and with whoever is not here with us the day.

en.L: but with whoever is here with us, standing today before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, and with whoever is not here with us today.
en.B: but with those who are standing here with us today before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, and also with those who are not with us here today.
en.R: I am making it with all of us who are standing here today in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. And I am also making it with those who are not here with us today.

es.L: sino con el que está aquí con nosotros, de pie hoy delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} nuestro Dios, y con el que no está aquí hoy con nosotros.
es.B: sino con los que están hoy aquí con nosotros delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} nuestro Dios, y también con los que no están hoy aquí con nosotros.
es.R: Lo hago con todos nosotros, los que estamos aquí hoy de pie ante {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios. Y lo hago también con los que no están hoy aquí con nosotros.

fr.L: mais avec celui qui est ici avec nous, se tenant aujourd’hui devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu, et avec celui qui n’est pas ici avec nous aujourd’hui.
fr.B: mais avec ceux qui se tiennent ici avec nous aujourd’hui devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu, et aussi avec ceux qui ne sont pas ici avec nous aujourd’hui.
fr.R: Je la conclus avec nous tous qui nous tenons ici aujourd’hui devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu. Et je la conclus aussi avec ceux qui ne sont pas ici avec nous aujourd’hui.

sw.L: bali pamoja na yeye aliye hapa pamoja nasi, akisimama leo mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu, na pamoja na yeye asiye hapa pamoja nasi leo.
sw.B: bali pamoja na wale waliosimama hapa pamoja nasi leo mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu, na pia pamoja na wale wasiokuwa hapa pamoja nasi leo.
sw.R: Ninalifanya pamoja na sisi sote tuliosimama hapa leo mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu. Tena ninalifanya pamoja na wale ambao hawapo hapa pamoja nasi leo.

decisions.choice: those not here today: the generations still to come
decisions.reason: The covenant binds not only the people present but those not yet born, their descendants. Verse 21 speaks of "the generation to come, your children who rise up after you", and 5:3 makes the same point the other way round: the covenant at Horeb was made "with us, all of us here alive today". Each generation stands under the covenant as if it had been there.

decisions.choice: whoever is here: one who is present
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a word for "there is" with "him": "the one who is here". The singular names each person present, and together they are the whole assembly.

decisions.choice: I am making it with ... And I am also making it with
decisions.reason: Readable repeats the verb from verse 13 so that each sentence can stand on its own.

source.text: כִּֽי־אַתֶּ֣ם יְדַעְתֶּ֔ם אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־יָשַׁ֖בְנוּ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְאֵ֧ת אֲשֶׁר־עָבַ֛רְנוּ בְּקֶ֥רֶב הַגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲבַרְתֶּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For you, you know how we lived in [the] land of Egypt and how we passed through [the] midst of the nations which you passed through.

en.L: For you yourselves know how we lived in the land of Egypt and how we passed through the midst of the nations through which you passed.
en.B: You yourselves know how we lived in Egypt and how we made our way through the nations along the route you took.
en.R: You know how we lived in Egypt. You know how we traveled through the lands of other nations on our way here.

es.L: Porque {{plural_you:ustedes saben|vosotros sabéis}} cómo habitamos en la tierra de Egipto y cómo pasamos por en medio de las naciones por las que {{plural_you:pasaron|pasasteis}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes mismos saben|Vosotros mismos sabéis}} cómo vivimos en Egipto y cómo nos abrimos paso entre las naciones por el camino que {{plural_you:siguieron|seguisteis}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes saben|Vosotros sabéis}} cómo vivimos en Egipto. {{plural_you:Saben|Sabéis}} cómo atravesamos las tierras de otras naciones en el camino hasta aquí.

fr.L: Car vous, vous savez comment nous avons habité au pays d’Égypte et comment nous sommes passés au milieu des nations que vous avez traversées.
fr.B: Vous savez vous-mêmes comment nous avons vécu en Égypte et comment nous avons fait route à travers les nations, par le chemin que vous avez suivi.
fr.R: Vous savez comment nous avons vécu en Égypte. Vous savez comment nous avons traversé les pays d’autres nations pour arriver jusqu’ici.

sw.L: Kwa maana ninyi mnajua jinsi tulivyokaa katika nchi ya Misri, na jinsi tulivyopita katikati ya mataifa mliyoyapitia.
sw.B: Ninyi wenyewe mnajua jinsi tulivyoishi Misri, na jinsi tulivyosafiri kupitia mataifa katika njia mliyoifuata.
sw.R: Mnajua jinsi tulivyoishi Misri. Mnajua jinsi tulivyopita katika nchi za mataifa mengine tulipokuwa tukija hapa.

decisions.choice: for you know: the reason for the warning that follows
decisions.reason: The word "for" leads into verses 15-17. Israel knows the gods of Egypt and of the nations along the way, and has seen their idols (verse 16). That is why the warning against turning to them follows in verse 17.

decisions.choice: the nations you passed through: Edom, Moab, Ammon and the Amorites
decisions.reason: On the way from Egypt Israel passed by or through the lands of Edom, Moab and Ammon and the kingdoms of Sihon and Og (2:1-3:11; Numbers 20-21). At Baal-peor in Moab many Israelites had already joined in the worship of a foreign god (4:3; Numbers 25:1-3).

decisions.choice: on our way here
decisions.reason: Readable leaves out the repeated "which you passed through" and says instead that the journey led to where they now stand.

source.text: וַתִּרְאוּ֙ אֶת־שִׁקּ֣וּצֵיהֶ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת גִּלֻּלֵיהֶ֑ם עֵ֣ץ וָאֶ֔בֶן כֶּ֥סֶף וְזָהָ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר עִמָּהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you saw their detestable things and their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, which [were] with them.

en.L: And you saw their detestable things and their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, which [were] among them.
en.B: You saw their detestable things and their idols of wood and stone, of silver and gold, that they had among them.
en.R: You saw their disgusting idols made of wood and stone, of silver and gold.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:vieron|visteis}} sus cosas detestables y sus ídolos, madera y piedra, plata y oro, que [había] entre ellos.
es.B: {{plural_you:Vieron|Visteis}} sus cosas detestables y sus ídolos de madera y de piedra, de plata y de oro, que tenían entre ellos.
es.R: {{plural_you:Vieron|Visteis}} sus ídolos repugnantes, hechos de madera y piedra, de plata y oro.

fr.L: Et vous avez vu leurs choses détestables et leurs idoles, de bois et de pierre, d’argent et d’or, qui [étaient] chez eux.
fr.B: Vous avez vu leurs choses détestables et leurs idoles de bois et de pierre, d’argent et d’or, qu’ils avaient chez eux.
fr.R: Vous avez vu leurs idoles dégoûtantes, faites de bois et de pierre, d’argent et d’or.

sw.L: Nanyi mliona machukizo yao na sanamu zao, za mti na jiwe, za fedha na dhahabu, zilizokuwa kwao.
sw.B: Mliona machukizo yao na sanamu zao za mti na za mawe, za fedha na za dhahabu, walizokuwa nazo.
sw.R: Mliona sanamu zao za kinyaa, zilizotengenezwa kwa mti na mawe, kwa fedha na dhahabu.

decisions.choice: detestable things: objects of worship that God hates
decisions.reason: The word names something loathsome and filthy, and it is used most often of the idols of other nations and their worship (1 Kings 11:5, 7; 2 Kings 23:13). Moses calls them what they are in God's eyes.

decisions.choice: idols: a scornful word for false gods
decisions.reason: The word for idols here may come from a root meaning to roll, and it may have reminded hearers of a word for dung, so that it mocks the images as lumps of filth. It is used most often by Ezekiel (Ezekiel 6:4-6), and in the Torah also in Leviticus 26:30.

decisions.choice: wood and stone, silver and gold: images made by hand
decisions.reason: Idols were carved from wood or stone, or cast and overlaid with silver and gold. Moses stresses that they were made things, "the work of human hands, wood and stone" (4:28).

decisions.choice: disgusting idols
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two nouns into one phrase, since both name the idols, and says "disgusting" for "detestable". Literal and Balanced keep both nouns.

source.text: פֶּן־יֵ֣שׁ בָּ֠כֶם אִ֣ישׁ אוֹ־אִשָּׁ֞ה א֧וֹ מִשְׁפָּחָ֣ה אוֹ־שֵׁ֗בֶט אֲשֶׁר֩ לְבָב֨וֹ פֹנֶ֤ה הַיּוֹם֙ מֵעִם֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ לָלֶ֣כֶת לַעֲבֹ֔ד אֶת־אֱלֹהֵ֖י הַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָהֵ֑ם פֶּן־יֵ֣שׁ בָּכֶ֗ם שֹׁ֛רֶשׁ פֹּרֶ֥ה רֹ֖אשׁ וְלַעֲנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Lest there be among you a man or a woman or a clan or a tribe whose heart [is] turning the day from with Yahweh our God, to go to serve [the] gods of the nations the those; lest there be among you a root bearing poison and wormwood.

en.L: [Beware] lest there be among you a man or a woman or a clan or a tribe whose heart is turning away today from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, to go and serve the gods of those nations; lest there be among you a root bearing poison and wormwood.
en.B: Make sure there is no man or woman, no clan or tribe among you, whose heart turns away today from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God and goes off to serve the gods of those nations. Let no root grow among you that bears poison and bitter fruit.
en.R: Make sure that no man or woman, no family or tribe among you, turns away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God today to worship the gods of those nations. Such people are like a root that grows a poisonous and bitter plant.

es.L: [{{plural_you:Cuídense|Cuidaos}}] de que no haya entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} hombre ni mujer, ni clan ni tribu cuyo corazón se aparte hoy {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} nuestro Dios para ir a servir a los dioses de aquellas naciones; de que no haya entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} raíz que dé veneno y ajenjo.
es.B: {{plural_you:Asegúrense|Aseguraos}} de que no haya entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} hombre ni mujer, clan ni tribu, cuyo corazón se aparte hoy {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} nuestro Dios y se vaya a servir a los dioses de esas naciones. Que no crezca entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} ninguna raíz que dé veneno y fruto amargo.
es.R: {{plural_you:Asegúrense|Aseguraos}} de que nadie entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, ni hombre ni mujer, ni familia ni tribu, se aparte hoy {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} nuestro Dios para adorar a los dioses de esas naciones. Gente así es como una raíz que produce una planta venenosa y amarga.

fr.L: [Prenez garde] qu’il n’y ait parmi vous homme ou femme, clan ou tribu dont le cœur se détourne aujourd’hui {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} notre Dieu pour aller servir les dieux de ces nations ; qu’il n’y ait parmi vous aucune racine qui porte du poison et de l’absinthe.
fr.B: Veillez à ce qu’il n’y ait parmi vous ni homme ni femme, ni clan ni tribu, dont le cœur se détourne aujourd’hui {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} notre Dieu pour aller servir les dieux de ces nations. Qu’aucune racine ne pousse parmi vous, qui porte du poison et des fruits amers.
fr.R: Faites bien attention : que personne parmi vous, homme ou femme, famille ou tribu, ne se détourne aujourd’hui {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} notre Dieu pour adorer les dieux de ces nations. De telles personnes sont comme une racine qui donne une plante empoisonnée et amère.

sw.L: [Jihadharini] asiwepo kati yenu mwanamume au mwanamke, au ukoo au kabila, ambaye moyo wake unageuka leo kumwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu, aende kuitumikia miungu ya mataifa hayo; pasiwepo kati yenu mzizi uzaao sumu na pakanga.
sw.B: Hakikisheni kwamba hakuna kati yenu mwanamume au mwanamke, ukoo au kabila, ambaye moyo wake unamwacha leo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu na kwenda kuitumikia miungu ya mataifa hayo. Pasiwe kati yenu mzizi unaozaa sumu na matunda machungu.
sw.R: Hakikisheni kwamba hakuna mtu kati yenu, mwanamume au mwanamke, ukoo au kabila, atakayemwacha leo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu ili kuabudu miungu ya mataifa hayo. Watu kama hao ni kama mzizi unaotoa mmea wenye sumu na uchungu.

decisions.choice: lest: a warning, beware that there is not
decisions.reason: The word means "so that not" or "lest". Here it stands at the start of the sentence without a verb before it and works as a warning: take care that there is no such person among you.

decisions.choice: whose heart turns away from the LORD: who inwardly stops being loyal to him
decisions.reason: The heart is the inner self, mind and will. A heart that turns from God has already left him before any act of worship of another god (11:16; 30:17). The danger can begin in one person and spread to a clan or a whole tribe.

decisions.choice: a root bearing poison and wormwood: a hidden source of deadly growth
decisions.reason: A root lies under the ground and is not seen, yet it bears fruit. The person who turns from God is pictured as such a root, whose fruit is poison for the whole people. "Poison" names a poisonous plant, perhaps the poppy or hemlock; wormwood is a plant known for its bitter taste (Amos 6:12; Jeremiah 9:14). The letter to the Hebrews draws on this verse (Hebrews 12:15).

decisions.choice: [Beware] lest
decisions.reason: Literal supplies "beware" in brackets, since the warning has no verb before "lest" in Hebrew.

decisions.choice: bitter fruit / bitter plant
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what wormwood is, a bitter plant, rather than its name. Literal keeps "wormwood".

decisions.choice: Such people are like a root
decisions.reason: Readable states the picture as a comparison and names who the root is, the people just described. The Hebrew sets the two warnings side by side and leaves the link to be seen.

decisions.choice: pakanga
decisions.reason: "Pakanga" is the name Swahili Bible readers know for wormwood, the bitter plant (it is the name of the star in Revelation 8:11). Literal keeps the plant's name, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable say what it is, something bitter.

source.text: וְהָיָ֡ה בְּשָׁמְעוֹ֩ אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֨י הָֽאָלָ֜ה הַזֹּ֗את וְהִתְבָּרֵ֨ךְ בִּלְבָב֤וֹ לֵאמֹר֙ שָׁל֣וֹם יִֽהְיֶה־לִּ֔י כִּ֛י בִּשְׁרִר֥וּת לִבִּ֖י אֵלֵ֑ךְ לְמַ֛עַן סְפ֥וֹת הָרָוָ֖ה אֶת־הַצְּמֵאָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, when he hears [the] words of the oath the this, and he blesses himself in his heart, saying, peace will be to me, though in [the] stubbornness of my heart I walk, so as to sweep away the watered with the thirsty.

en.L: And it will be, when he hears the words of this oath, that he will bless himself in his heart, saying, 'I will have peace, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart,' so as to sweep away the watered [land] with the dry.
en.B: When such a person hears the words of this oath, they may congratulate themselves in their heart and think, 'I will be safe, even though I follow my own stubborn heart.' That would bring ruin on the watered land and the dry alike.
en.R: Such a person may hear the words of this solemn oath and still feel sure of being blessed. They may think, 'I will be safe, even if I do whatever my stubborn heart wants.' But that would destroy everything, the good with the bad.

es.L: Y sucederá que, cuando oiga las palabras de este juramento, se bendecirá en su corazón, diciendo: “Tendré paz, aunque ande en la terquedad de mi corazón”, para arrasar la [tierra] regada junto con la seca.
es.B: Cuando una persona así oiga las palabras de este juramento, puede felicitarse en su interior y pensar: “Estaré a salvo, aunque siga mi corazón obstinado”. Eso traería la ruina sobre la tierra regada y la seca por igual.
es.R: Esa persona puede oír las palabras de este juramento solemne y aun así sentirse segura de que será bendecida. Puede pensar: “Estaré a salvo aunque haga todo lo que quiera mi terco corazón”. Pero eso lo destruiría todo, lo bueno junto con lo malo.

fr.L: Et il arrivera, quand il entendra les paroles de ce serment, qu’il se bénira dans son cœur en disant : “J’aurai la paix, même si je marche dans l’obstination de mon cœur”, de sorte qu’il emporte la [terre] arrosée avec la sèche.
fr.B: Quand une telle personne entendra les paroles de ce serment, elle risque de se féliciter en elle-même et de penser : “Tout ira bien pour moi, même si je suis mon cœur obstiné.” Cela mènerait à la ruine la terre arrosée comme la terre sèche.
fr.R: Une telle personne peut entendre les paroles de ce serment solennel et se croire quand même bénie. Elle peut penser : “Je serai en sécurité, même si je fais tout ce que veut mon cœur têtu.” Mais cela détruirait tout, le bon avec le mauvais.

sw.L: Na itakuwa, atakaposikia maneno ya kiapo hiki, atajibariki moyoni mwake, akisema, 'Nitakuwa na amani, ingawa ninaenenda katika ukaidi wa moyo wangu,' hata kufagilia mbali [nchi] iliyonyweshwa pamoja na iliyokauka.
sw.B: Mtu wa namna hiyo akisikia maneno ya kiapo hiki, anaweza kujipongeza moyoni mwake na kuwaza, 'Nitakuwa salama, hata nikifuata ukaidi wa moyo wangu.' Jambo hilo lingeleta maangamizi juu ya nchi iliyonyweshwa na iliyokauka vilevile.
sw.R: Mtu kama huyo anaweza kusikia maneno ya kiapo hiki kizito na bado akajiona amebarikiwa. Anaweza kuwaza, 'Nitakuwa salama hata nikifanya chochote ambacho moyo wangu mkaidi unataka.' Lakini hilo lingeangamiza kila kitu, kizuri pamoja na kibaya.

decisions.choice: bless himself in his heart: tell himself that he is safe
decisions.reason: The verb means to bless oneself, to count oneself blessed. On hearing the curses of the covenant the man assures himself that they will not touch him. "In his heart" means in his own mind, not aloud (Isaiah 65:16; Psalm 49:19).

decisions.choice: peace: safety and well-being; stubbornness: going one's own way against God
decisions.reason: "Peace will be to me" means "all will be well with me" (Jeremiah 23:17). The word for stubbornness is used almost only by Jeremiah (Jeremiah 7:24; 9:13; 13:10), for a heart set on its own way against God's word.

decisions.choice: to sweep away the watered with the dry: probably, to bring ruin on everything
alternatives: it is part of what the man says to himself
the guilty and the innocent alike
decisions.reason: The phrase is hard. "The watered" and "the thirsty" are feminine and probably mean watered and dry ground, a pair that stands for everything together, good and bad alike. On this reading the man's self-deceit brings destruction on the whole land, not on himself alone, as verse 17 warns and verses 21-27 describe. Others take the words to mean adding drunkenness to thirst, or the moist plant with the dry, so that he destroys himself completely. The phrase may also be the man's own words, a careless saying that the rest of his life will go as it will. The text does not decide.

decisions.choice: he ... me: the man or woman of verse 17
decisions.reason: The pronouns are masculine singular, as Hebrew uses for anyone, but they refer back to the person of verse 17, man or woman.

decisions.choice: such a person ... they
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "such a person" and use "they" and "themselves", since verse 17 names a man or a woman. Literal keeps "he" and "his".

decisions.choice: bring ruin on the watered land and the dry alike / destroy everything, the good with the bad
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the likely reading with the words of the picture; Readable gives its meaning in plain words. Both choose the reading in the meaning note, which is uncertain.

decisions.choice: une telle personne ... elle
decisions.reason: Verse 17 names a man or a woman, so Balanced and Readable speak of "une telle personne", which takes "elle" in French without pointing to a woman. Literal keeps "il", as the Hebrew has.

source.text: לֹא־יֹאבֶ֣ה יְהוָה֮ סְלֹ֣חַֽ לוֹ֒ כִּ֣י אָ֠ז יֶעְשַׁ֨ן אַף־יְהוָ֤ה וְקִנְאָתוֹ֙ בָּאִ֣ישׁ הַה֔וּא וְרָ֤בְצָה בּוֹ֙ כָּל־הָ֣אָלָ֔ה הַכְּתוּבָ֖ה בַּסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֑ה וּמָחָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֶת־שְׁמ֔וֹ מִתַּ֖חַת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: Not will be willing Yahweh to forgive him, for then will smoke [the] anger of Yahweh and his jealousy against the man the that, and will lie down on him all the oath the written in the book the this, and will wipe out Yahweh his name from under the heavens.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will not be willing to forgive him, for then the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} jealousy will smoke against that man, and every curse written in this book will lie down upon him, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will blot out his name from under heaven.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will not be willing to forgive that person. Instead, the anger and jealousy of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will burn like fire against them, and every curse written in this book will settle on them, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will wipe out their name from under heaven.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will never be willing to forgive that person. The anger and jealousy of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will blaze up against them. Every curse written in this book will fall on them, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will wipe out every memory of them from the earth.

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no querrá perdonarlo, porque entonces humeará la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} celo contra ese hombre, y toda maldición escrita en este libro se echará sobre él, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} borrará su nombre de debajo del cielo.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no querrá perdonar a esa persona. Al contrario, la ira y el celo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} arderán como fuego contra ella, todas las maldiciones escritas en este libro se asentarán sobre ella, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} borrará su nombre de debajo del cielo.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nunca querrá perdonar a esa persona. La ira y el celo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se encenderán contra ella. Todas las maldiciones escritas en este libro caerán sobre ella, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} borrará de la tierra todo recuerdo de ella.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne voudra pas lui pardonner, car alors la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} jalousie fumeront contre cet homme, et toute la malédiction écrite dans ce livre se couchera sur lui, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} effacera son nom de dessous le ciel.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne voudra pas pardonner à cette personne. Au contraire, la colère et la jalousie {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’enflammeront contre elle, toutes les malédictions écrites dans ce livre reposeront sur elle, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} effacera son nom de dessous le ciel.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne voudra jamais pardonner à cette personne. La colère et la jalousie {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’embraseront contre elle. Toutes les malédictions écrites dans ce livre tomberont sur elle, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} effacera de la terre tout souvenir d’elle.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hatakuwa radhi kumsamehe, kwa maana hapo hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na wivu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} vitafuka moshi juu ya mtu huyo, na laana yote iliyoandikwa katika kitabu hiki italala juu yake, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atalifuta jina lake kutoka chini ya mbingu.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hatakubali kumsamehe mtu huyo. Badala yake, hasira na wivu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} vitawaka kama moto juu yake, kila laana iliyoandikwa katika kitabu hiki itatua juu yake, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atalifuta jina lake chini ya mbingu.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hatakubali kamwe kumsamehe mtu huyo. Hasira na wivu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} vitawaka juu yake. Kila laana iliyoandikwa katika kitabu hiki itamwangukia, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atafuta kabisa kumbukumbu lake duniani.

decisions.choice: the anger of the LORD will smoke: his anger will flare up
decisions.reason: Anger is pictured as fire and its smoke, as in Psalm 74:1 and 80:5. "Jealousy" is God's zeal for the loyalty he is owed, the jealousy of 4:24 and 5:9, which will not share his people with other gods.

decisions.choice: every curse ... will lie down on him: the curses will settle on him and stay
decisions.reason: The word translated "curse" is the same as "oath" in verses 11, 13 and 18: the oath brings its curses on whoever breaks it. "Lie down" is used of an animal crouching at rest (Genesis 49:9); the curses come to rest on the man and do not leave.

decisions.choice: blot out his name from under heaven: leave no one and nothing to remember him
decisions.reason: A person's name lived on in his descendants and in the memory of his people. To blot it out is to end his line and his memory completely (9:14; 25:6, 19; Exodus 17:14).

decisions.choice: will not be willing to forgive: will refuse to pardon
decisions.reason: The man who hoped to be safe (verse 18) will find no pardon. The same verb is used in 1:26 of Israel's refusal to go up into the land and in 10:10 of the LORD's unwillingness to destroy them.

decisions.choice: that person ... them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable continue from verse 18 with "that person" and "they", since a man or a woman is meant (verse 17). Literal keeps "that man" and "him", as the Hebrew has.

decisions.choice: burn like fire
decisions.reason: Balanced says "burn like fire" for "smoke", keeping the picture of fire without the unusual verb. Readable says "blaze up".

decisions.choice: wipe out every memory of them from the earth
decisions.reason: Readable says what blotting out a name means, and "from the earth" for "from under heaven", everywhere people live.

source.text: וְהִבְדִּיל֤וֹ יְהוָה֙ לְרָעָ֔ה מִכֹּ֖ל שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כְּכֹל֙ אָל֣וֹת הַבְּרִ֔ית הַכְּתוּבָ֕ה בְּסֵ֥פֶר הַתּוֹרָ֖ה הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will separate him Yahweh for evil from all [the] tribes of Israel according to all [the] oaths of the covenant the written in [the] book of the law the this.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will set him apart for harm from all the tribes of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant written in this book of the law.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will single them out from all the tribes of Israel for disaster, in keeping with all the covenant curses written in this book of the law.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will pick that person out from all the tribes of Israel to be punished. It will happen just as all the curses of the covenant in this book of teaching say.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo apartará para el mal de entre todas las tribus de Israel, conforme a todas las maldiciones del pacto escritas en este libro de la ley.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} apartará a esa persona de entre todas las tribus de Israel para la desgracia, conforme a todas las maldiciones del pacto escritas en este libro de la ley.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} escogerá a esa persona de entre todas las tribus de Israel para castigarla. Sucederá tal como dicen todas las maldiciones del pacto que están en este libro de enseñanza.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} le séparera de toutes les tribus d’Israël pour le malheur, selon toutes les malédictions de l’alliance écrites dans ce livre de la loi.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} mettra cette personne à part, parmi toutes les tribus d’Israël, pour la frapper de malheur, conformément à toutes les malédictions de l’alliance écrites dans ce livre de la loi.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} choisira cette personne parmi toutes les tribus d’Israël pour la punir. Tout se passera comme le disent les malédictions de l’alliance écrites dans ce livre d’enseignement.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamtenga kwa ajili ya mabaya kutoka katika makabila yote ya Israeli, kwa kufuata laana zote za agano zilizoandikwa katika kitabu hiki cha sheria.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamtenga mtu huyo kutoka katika makabila yote ya Israeli ili apatwe na maafa, kwa mujibu wa laana zote za agano zilizoandikwa katika kitabu hiki cha sheria.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamchagua mtu huyo kutoka katika makabila yote ya Israeli ili aadhibiwe. Itakuwa sawasawa na laana zote za agano zilizo katika kitabu hiki cha mafundisho.

decisions.choice: set him apart for harm: single him out for disaster
decisions.reason: The verb means to separate or set apart, the same word used of setting the Levites apart for God's service (10:8). Here the man is set apart from his people for ruin. The punishment falls on him in particular, not on the tribes he is taken from.

decisions.choice: the curses of the covenant: the penalties sworn for breaking it
decisions.reason: The word is the plural of the word for "oath" in verses 11-19: the sworn curses written in the covenant, as listed in 27:15-26 and 28:15-68.

decisions.choice: the book of the law: the written record of Moses' teaching
decisions.reason: "Law" here is the whole of what Moses teaches, instruction as well as rules (1:5). Moses writes it down in 31:9, 24-26, and it is to be kept beside the ark.

decisions.choice: them / that person
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable go on with "them" or "that person", as in verses 18-19. Literal keeps "him".

decisions.choice: this book of teaching
decisions.reason: Readable says "teaching" for the word Literal and Balanced render "law", as Deuteronomy does at Readable (see 1:5).

source.text: וְאָמַ֞ר הַדּ֣וֹר הָֽאַחֲר֗וֹן בְּנֵיכֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָק֨וּמוּ֙ מֵאַ֣חֲרֵיכֶ֔ם וְהַ֨נָּכְרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָבֹ֖א מֵאֶ֣רֶץ רְחוֹקָ֑ה וְ֠רָאוּ אֶת־מַכּ֞וֹת הָאָ֤רֶץ הַהִוא֙ וְאֶת־תַּ֣חֲלֻאֶ֔יהָ אֲשֶׁר־חִלָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה בָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will say the generation the later, your children who will rise from after you, and the foreigner who will come from a land distant, and they will see [the] plagues of the land the that and its diseases with which has made sick Yahweh it,

en.L: And the generation to come, your children who rise up after you, and the foreigner who comes from a distant land, will say, when they see the plagues of that land and its diseases with which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has made it sick,
en.B: In time to come your children, the generation who rise up after you, will speak of it, and so will foreigners who come from a distant land, when they see the plagues of that land and the sicknesses {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has struck it with,
en.R: In the future your children who come after you will see the plagues of that land and the diseases {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent on it. Foreigners who come from distant countries will see them too.

es.L: Y dirá la generación venidera, {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}} que se levanten después de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y el extranjero que venga de tierra lejana, cuando vean las plagas de aquella tierra y las enfermedades con que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} la ha hecho enfermar,
es.B: En el futuro, {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}}, la generación que se levante después de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hablarán de ello, y también los extranjeros que vengan de tierras lejanas, cuando vean las plagas de aquella tierra y las enfermedades con que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} la ha herido,
es.R: En el futuro, {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}}, los que vengan después de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, verán las plagas de aquella tierra y las enfermedades que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha enviado sobre ella. También las verán los extranjeros que vengan de países lejanos.

fr.L: Et la génération à venir, vos enfants qui se lèveront après vous, et l’étranger qui viendra d’un pays lointain diront, quand ils verront les plaies de ce pays et les maladies dont {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’a frappé,
fr.B: À l’avenir, vos enfants, la génération qui se lèvera après vous, en parleront, et de même les étrangers venus d’un pays lointain, quand ils verront les plaies de ce pays et les maladies dont {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’aura frappé,
fr.R: Plus tard, vos enfants, qui viendront après vous, verront les fléaux qui frappent ce pays et les maladies que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a envoyées. Les étrangers venus de pays lointains les verront aussi.

sw.L: Na kizazi kijacho, watoto wenu watakaoinuka baada yenu, na mtu wa kigeni atakayekuja kutoka nchi ya mbali, watasema, watakapoyaona mapigo ya nchi ile na magonjwa ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameiletea,
sw.B: Siku zijazo watoto wenu, kizazi kitakachoinuka baada yenu, watazungumza juu yake, na vivyo hivyo watu wa mataifa mengine watakaokuja kutoka nchi za mbali, watakapoyaona mapigo ya nchi ile na maradhi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameipiga nayo,
sw.R: Siku zijazo watoto wenu watakaokuja baada yenu wataona mapigo ya nchi ile na magonjwa ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameyaleta juu yake. Watu wa mataifa mengine watakaotoka nchi za mbali watayaona pia.

decisions.choice: will say ... when they see: the words they say follow in verse 23
decisions.reason: The sentence names the speakers and what they see, and then describes the ruined land in verse 22. What they say is given in verse 23, where "all the nations" join them in asking why. The "later generation" is Israel's own descendants; the foreigner is any traveler from far away.

decisions.choice: the plagues of that land: the land itself under the covenant curses
decisions.reason: The land is pictured as a sick body struck down by the LORD, as the curses of 28:21-22, 59-61 threatened the people. "That land" is the land of Israel as it will look after the covenant is broken. Moses now turns from the one guilty person (verses 17-20) to the whole nation.

decisions.choice: will speak of it
decisions.reason: Balanced says "will speak of it" for "will say", since the words they say do not come until verse 23. Literal keeps "will say".

decisions.choice: will see ... will see them too
decisions.reason: Readable leaves "will say" for verse 23, where it gives what they say, and makes two sentences about what they see.

source.text: גָּפְרִ֣ית וָמֶלַח֮ שְׂרֵפָ֣ה כָל־אַרְצָהּ֒ לֹ֤א תִזָּרַע֙ וְלֹ֣א תַצְמִ֔חַ וְלֹֽא־יַעֲלֶ֥ה בָ֖הּ כָּל־עֵ֑שֶׂב כְּֽמַהְפֵּכַ֞ת סְדֹ֤ם וַעֲמֹרָה֙ אַדְמָ֣ה וּצְבוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הָפַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה בְּאַפּ֖וֹ וּבַחֲמָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: sulfur and salt, a burning [is] all its land; not it will be sown and not it will sprout and not will come up on it any plant, like [the] overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which overthrew Yahweh in his anger and in his wrath,

en.L: its whole land sulfur and salt, a burning; it is not sown, and it does not sprout, and no plant comes up on it, like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} overthrew in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger and in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wrath,
en.B: the whole land burned out with sulfur and salt, nothing sown, nothing sprouting, no plant coming up in it, like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} overthrew them in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger and fury,
en.R: They will see that the whole land is a burned waste of sulfur and salt. Nothing is planted there, and nothing grows. Not even a weed comes up. It will be like Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, the cities {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} destroyed when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was very angry.

es.L: azufre y sal, quemazón [es] toda su tierra; no se siembra, ni hace brotar, ni crece en ella hierba alguna, como en la destrucción de Sodoma y Gomorra, de Adma y Zeboim, que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} asoló en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira y en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} furor,
es.B: toda la tierra quemada por el azufre y la sal, nada sembrado, nada que brote, ni una planta que crezca en ella, como cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} destruyó Sodoma y Gomorra, Adma y Zeboim, en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} furor,
es.R: Verán que toda la tierra es un desierto quemado de azufre y sal. Allí no se siembra nada, y nada crece. Ni siquiera brota una mala hierba. Será como Sodoma y Gomorra, Adma y Zeboim, las ciudades que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} destruyó cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba muy enojado.

fr.L: tout son pays [n’est que] soufre et sel, une brûlure ; il n’est pas ensemencé, il ne fait rien germer, et aucune herbe n’y pousse, comme lors du bouleversement de Sodome et Gomorrhe, d’Adma et de Tseboïm, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a bouleversées dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère et dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} fureur,
fr.B: le pays tout entier brûlé par le soufre et le sel, rien de semé, rien qui germe, pas une plante qui y pousse, comme lorsque {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a renversé Sodome et Gomorrhe, Adma et Tseboïm, dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} fureur,
fr.R: Ils verront que tout le pays n’est plus qu’une terre brûlée, couverte de soufre et de sel. On n’y sème rien, et rien n’y germe. Il n’y pousse même pas une mauvaise herbe. Ce sera comme pour Sodome et Gomorrhe, Adma et Tseboïm, les villes que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a détruites quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était très en colère.

sw.L: nchi yake yote [ni] kiberiti na chumvi, moto; haipandwi, wala haichipushi, wala hakuna jani linalomea ndani yake, kama kupinduliwa kwa Sodoma na Gomora, Adma na Seboimu, [miji] ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliipindua katika hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na katika ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}},
sw.B: nchi yote imeteketezwa kwa kiberiti na chumvi, haipandwi kitu, hakuna kinachochipuka, wala hakuna mmea unaomea ndani yake, kama vile {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alipoipindua Sodoma na Gomora, Adma na Seboimu, katika hasira na ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}},
sw.R: Wataona kwamba nchi yote ni jangwa lililoungua kwa kiberiti na chumvi. Hakuna kinachopandwa huko, wala hakuna kinachomea. Hata magugu hayamei. Itakuwa kama Sodoma na Gomora, Adma na Seboimu, miji ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliiangamiza alipokasirika sana.

decisions.choice: sulfur and salt, a burning: land made useless for farming
decisions.reason: Sulfur, which burns, and salt, which kills plants and spoils the soil, describe land left barren like the area around the Dead Sea. Salt was sometimes sown on a conquered city to curse it (Judges 9:45). The land that once flowed with milk and honey becomes a waste (compare Jeremiah 17:6; Zephaniah 2:9).

decisions.choice: like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim
decisions.reason: Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed by fire and sulfur from the LORD (Genesis 19:24-25). Admah and Zeboiim were two other cities of the plain, named with them in Genesis 10:19 and 14:2, and remembered with them in Hosea 11:8. Their ruin became the standard picture of total judgment (Isaiah 1:9; Amos 4:11).

decisions.choice: Zeboiim: the name is written one way and read another
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text spell the name slightly differently from the way the scribes' marginal note says to read it. Both forms name the same city; the meaning is not affected.

decisions.choice: They will see ... Not even a weed comes up
decisions.reason: Readable begins with "They will see" to link the description to verse 21, and says "not even a weed" for "no plant", to stress that nothing at all grows.

decisions.choice: the cities the LORD destroyed when he was very angry
decisions.reason: Readable says "destroyed" for "overthrew" and joins "in his anger and in his wrath" into "very angry", since the two words mean much the same and together stress how great the anger was.

source.text: וְאָֽמְרוּ֙ כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם עַל־מֶ֨ה עָשָׂ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה כָּ֖כָה לָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את מֶ֥ה חֳרִ֛י הָאַ֥ף הַגָּד֖וֹל הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and will say all the nations, for what has done Yahweh thus to the land the this? What [is] the heat of the anger the great the this?

en.L: and all the nations will say, 'Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} done thus to this land? What [is] the heat of this great anger?'
en.B: and all the nations will ask, 'Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} done this to this land? Why this fierce and terrible anger?'
en.R: People from all the nations will ask, 'Why did {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} do this to this land? Why was {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} so terribly angry?'

es.L: y dirán todas las naciones: “¿Por qué hizo así {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a esta tierra? ¿Qué [es] el ardor de esta gran ira?”.
es.B: y todas las naciones preguntarán: “¿Por qué ha hecho esto {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} con esta tierra? ¿Por qué una ira tan feroz y terrible?”.
es.R: La gente de todas las naciones preguntará: “¿Por qué hizo esto {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} con esta tierra? ¿Por qué se enojó tanto?”.

fr.L: et toutes les nations diront : “Pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a-t-il agi ainsi envers ce pays ? Que [signifie] l’ardeur de cette grande colère ?”
fr.B: et toutes les nations demanderont : “Pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a-t-il traité ce pays de cette façon ? Pourquoi une colère si violente et si terrible ?”
fr.R: Les gens de toutes les nations demanderont : “Pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a-t-il fait cela à ce pays ? Pourquoi s’est-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} tellement mis en colère ?”

sw.L: na mataifa yote yatasema, 'Kwa nini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameifanyia nchi hii hivi? Ni nini ukali wa hasira hii kuu?'
sw.B: na mataifa yote yatauliza, 'Kwa nini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameitendea nchi hii hivi? Kwa nini hasira hii kali na ya kutisha?'
sw.R: Watu wa mataifa yote watauliza, 'Kwa nini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliifanyia nchi hii jambo hili? Kwa nini alikasirika vibaya hivyo?'

decisions.choice: all the nations will say: the question of verse 21's speakers, now joined by everyone
decisions.reason: Verse 21 named those who would speak, Israel's descendants and the foreigner. Here all the nations join them, and their question is given. The ruin of the land will be so great that the whole world will ask what caused it. The same question and answer come in 1 Kings 9:8-9 and Jeremiah 22:8-9.

decisions.choice: the heat of anger: fierce, burning anger
decisions.reason: Anger in Hebrew is pictured as heat and fire, and the "heat" of it is its fury. The question asks what could have made God so angry, not whether he was.

decisions.choice: ask
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ask" for "say", since what follows is a question.

decisions.choice: People from all the nations
decisions.reason: Readable says "people from" the nations, since it is people who will ask. The quotation is given single quotation marks because it stands inside Moses' speech.

source.text: וְאָ֣מְר֔וּ עַ֚ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָֽזְב֔וּ אֶת־בְּרִ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתָ֑ם אֲשֶׁר֙ כָּרַ֣ת עִמָּ֔ם בְּהוֹצִיא֥וֹ אֹתָ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will say, because they forsook [the] covenant of Yahweh, [the] God of their fathers, which he cut with them when he brought them out from [the] land of Egypt,

en.L: And they will say, 'Because they forsook the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their fathers, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made with them when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them out of the land of Egypt,
en.B: And the answer will be, 'It is because they left the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors, the covenant {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made with them when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led them out of Egypt,
en.R: And people will answer, 'It is because they turned their backs on the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors. He made that covenant with them when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them out of Egypt.

es.L: Y dirán: “Porque abandonaron el pacto {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, el Dios de sus padres, que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hizo con ellos cuando los sacó de la tierra de Egipto,
es.B: Y la respuesta será: “Es porque dejaron el pacto {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, el Dios de sus antepasados, el pacto que hizo con ellos cuando los sacó de Egipto,
es.R: Y la gente responderá: “Es porque le dieron la espalda al pacto {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, el Dios de sus antepasados. Ese pacto lo hizo con ellos cuando los sacó de Egipto.

fr.L: Et l’on dira : “Parce qu’ils ont abandonné l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, le Dieu de leurs pères, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait conclue avec eux quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a fait sortir du pays d’Égypte,
fr.B: Et on répondra : “C’est parce qu’ils ont délaissé l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, le Dieu de leurs ancêtres, l’alliance qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait conclue avec eux quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a conduits hors d’Égypte,
fr.R: Et on leur répondra : “C’est parce qu’ils ont tourné le dos à l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, le Dieu de leurs ancêtres. Il avait conclu cette alliance avec eux quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a fait sortir d’Égypte.

sw.L: Na watasema, 'Ni kwa sababu waliliacha agano la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa baba zao, alilofanya nao alipowatoa katika nchi ya Misri,
sw.B: Na jibu litakuwa, 'Ni kwa sababu waliliacha agano la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa mababu zao, agano alilofanya nao alipowaongoza kutoka Misri,
sw.R: Na watu watajibu, 'Ni kwa sababu walilipa kisogo agano la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa mababu zao. Alifanya agano hilo nao alipowatoa Misri.

decisions.choice: and they will say: an answer given by others
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. It means "people will say", the answer given to the nations' question. The answer runs through verse 27.

decisions.choice: forsook the covenant: abandoned the bond with God
decisions.reason: To forsake is to leave someone or something one belongs to. Israel will have walked away from the covenant God made with them at Sinai after the exodus, the bond that made them his people (28:20; 31:16; Jeremiah 22:9).

decisions.choice: the answer will be
decisions.reason: Balanced says "the answer will be" for "they will say", which has no named subject. Readable says "people will answer".

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ancestors" for "fathers", as in verse 12.

source.text: וַיֵּלְכ֗וּ וַיַּֽעַבְדוּ֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוּ֖וּלָהֶ֑ם אֱלֹהִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־יְדָע֔וּם וְלֹ֥א חָלַ֖ק לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and they went and served other gods and bowed down to them, gods whom not they had known them and not he had allotted to them.

en.L: and they went and served other gods and bowed down to them, gods whom they had not known and whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had not allotted to them.
en.B: and they went and served other gods and bowed down to them, gods they had never known and that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had not given them.
en.R: They went and worshiped other gods and bowed down to them. They did not know those gods, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had not given those gods to them.

es.L: y fueron y sirvieron a otros dioses y se postraron ante ellos, dioses que no habían conocido y que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no les había asignado.
es.B: y se fueron a servir a otros dioses y a postrarse ante ellos, dioses que nunca habían conocido y que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no les había dado.
es.R: Se fueron a adorar a otros dioses y se inclinaron ante ellos. No conocían a esos dioses, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no se los había dado.

fr.L: et ils sont allés, ils ont servi d’autres dieux et se sont prosternés devant eux, des dieux qu’ils n’avaient pas connus et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne leur avait pas attribués.
fr.B: et ils sont allés servir d’autres dieux et se prosterner devant eux, des dieux qu’ils n’avaient jamais connus et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne leur avait pas donnés.
fr.R: Ils sont allés adorer d’autres dieux et se sont inclinés devant eux. Ils ne connaissaient pas ces dieux, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne les leur avait pas donnés.

sw.L: wakaenda wakaitumikia miungu mingine na kuisujudia, miungu ambayo hawakuijua, wala hakuwagawia.
sw.B: wakaenda kuitumikia miungu mingine na kuisujudia, miungu ambayo hawakuwahi kuijua, wala hakuwapa.
sw.R: Walikwenda kuabudu miungu mingine na kuisujudia. Hawakuijua miungu hiyo, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakuwa amewapa miungu hiyo.

decisions.choice: served and bowed down: worshiped
decisions.reason: To serve a god and bow down to it is to worship it, the words of the second commandment (5:9). "Went" pictures Israel leaving the LORD to follow them (verse 17).

decisions.choice: gods they had not known: gods with whom they had no history
decisions.reason: Israel knew the LORD by what he had done for them (verses 1-7). The other gods had done nothing for them (11:28; 13:3; 32:17).

decisions.choice: gods he had not allotted to them: not given to Israel as their portion
alternatives: the gods had given Israel nothing
decisions.reason: The verb means to give out a share. In 4:19 Moses says the LORD "allotted" the sun, moon and stars to all the peoples, while Israel was taken as his own portion (4:20; 32:8-9). Israel's portion is the LORD himself, and these gods were never theirs. The subject "he" is the LORD, as in verse 24.

decisions.choice: the LORD had not given those gods to them
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD where the Hebrew has only "he", and repeats "those gods", so that each sentence is clear on its own.

source.text: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַהִ֑וא לְהָבִ֤יא עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַקְּלָלָ֔ה הַכְּתוּבָ֖ה בַּסֵּ֥פֶר הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And burned [the] anger of Yahweh against the land the that to bring on it all the curse the written in the book the this.

en.L: And the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against that land, to bring upon it every curse written in this book.
en.B: So the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against that land, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought on it every curse written in this book.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} became very angry with that land. He brought on it all the curses written in this book.

es.L: Y se encendió la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} contra aquella tierra, para traer sobre ella toda maldición escrita en este libro.
es.B: Por eso se encendió la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} contra aquella tierra, y trajo sobre ella todas las maldiciones escritas en este libro.
es.R: Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se enojó mucho con aquella tierra. Hizo caer sobre ella todas las maldiciones escritas en este libro.

fr.L: Et la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’est enflammée contre ce pays, pour faire venir sur lui toute la malédiction écrite dans ce livre.
fr.B: Alors la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’est enflammée contre ce pays, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait venir sur lui toutes les malédictions écrites dans ce livre.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} s’est mis très en colère contre ce pays. Il a fait tomber sur lui toutes les malédictions écrites dans ce livre.

sw.L: Na hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ikawaka juu ya nchi ile, ili kuleta juu yake kila laana iliyoandikwa katika kitabu hiki.
sw.B: Basi hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} iliwaka juu ya nchi ile, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akaleta juu yake kila laana iliyoandikwa katika kitabu hiki.
sw.R: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliikasirikia sana nchi ile. Akaleta juu yake laana zote zilizoandikwa katika kitabu hiki.

decisions.choice: the anger of the LORD burned: he became very angry
decisions.reason: The common Hebrew idiom pictures anger as heat that flares up (6:15; 7:4; 11:17).

decisions.choice: curse: the ordinary word for a curse
decisions.reason: Here the word is the usual one for a curse, the opposite of blessing (11:26-28; 28:15), not the word for "oath" of verses 19-20. Both refer to the same written penalties.

decisions.choice: written in this book: the curses Moses has set out
decisions.reason: The speakers of the future know "this book", the written law with its curses (28:58, 61). In their words the curses written there have come true.

decisions.choice: he brought on it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "to bring" into a second statement, with the LORD as subject, since the Hebrew phrase states the result of his anger.

source.text: וַיִּתְּשֵׁ֤ם יְהוָה֙ מֵעַ֣ל אַדְמָתָ֔ם בְּאַ֥ף וּבְחֵמָ֖ה וּבְקֶ֣צֶף גָּד֑וֹל וַיַּשְׁלִכֵ֛ם אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ אַחֶ֖רֶת כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And uprooted them Yahweh from on their land in anger and in rage and in wrath great, and he cast them into a land another, as the day the this.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} uprooted them from their land in anger and in rage and in great wrath, and cast them into another land, as [it is] this day.'
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} uprooted them from their land in anger, fury and great wrath, and threw them into another land, as it is today.'
en.R: So in great anger {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} pulled them up by the roots from their land. He threw them out into another land, where they are now.'

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los arrancó de su tierra con ira, con furor y con gran enojo, y los arrojó a otra tierra, como [sucede] hoy”.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los arrancó de su tierra con ira, furor y gran enojo, y los echó a otra tierra, como se ve hoy”.
es.R: Por eso, con gran enojo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los arrancó de raíz de su tierra. Los echó a otra tierra, donde están ahora”.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les a arrachés de leur sol dans la colère, dans la fureur et dans un grand courroux, et les a jetés dans un autre pays, comme [c’est le cas] aujourd’hui.”
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les a déracinés de leur terre avec colère, fureur et grand courroux, et les a rejetés dans un autre pays, comme on le voit aujourd’hui.”
fr.R: Alors, dans une grande colère, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les a arrachés de leur pays comme on arrache une plante avec ses racines. Il les a jetés dans un autre pays, où ils sont encore aujourd’hui.”

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawang'oa katika nchi yao kwa hasira, na kwa ukali, na kwa ghadhabu kuu, akawatupa katika nchi nyingine, kama [ilivyo] leo.'
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwang'oa katika nchi yao kwa hasira, ukali na ghadhabu kuu, akawatupa katika nchi nyingine, kama ilivyo leo.'
sw.R: Basi kwa hasira kubwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwang'oa katika nchi yao kama mmea unavyong'olewa pamoja na mizizi yake. Akawatupa katika nchi nyingine, mahali walipo sasa.'

decisions.choice: uprooted them from their land: removed them like a plant torn out of the ground
decisions.reason: Israel had been "planted" in the land (Exodus 15:17); to be uprooted is to be torn out and thrown away. The same picture is used of exile in 1 Kings 14:15 and Jeremiah 12:14-17. It fulfills the curse of 28:63-64.

decisions.choice: anger, rage and great wrath: three words for the fullness of God's anger
decisions.reason: The three nouns mean much the same; heaped together they show how great the anger is, as in Jeremiah 21:5 and 32:37.

decisions.choice: as it is this day: as it stands at the time of the speakers
decisions.reason: The words belong to the future speakers of verse 24, who see Israel in exile. From their point of view the uprooting has already happened and is still the case "today". This closes their answer.

decisions.choice: and cast them: written with an enlarged letter
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew text one letter of the word for "cast them" is written larger than the others, one of several enlarged letters the scribes preserved. Its purpose is unknown; it does not change the meaning.

decisions.choice: in great anger
decisions.reason: Readable joins the three words for anger into "great anger", and says "pulled them up by the roots" to make the picture plain.

decisions.choice: closing single quotation mark
decisions.reason: The answer that began in verse 24 ends here, so its single quotation mark closes. Moses' own speech, which opened in verse 1, goes on.

source.text: הַ֨נִּסְתָּרֹ֔ת לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וְהַנִּגְלֹ֞ת לָ֤ׄנׄוּׄוּׄלְׄבָׄנֵׄ֨יׄנׄוּׄ֙עַד־עוֹלָ֔ם לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת אֶת־כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֖י הַתּוֹרָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: The hidden [things belong] to Yahweh our God, and the revealed [things belong] to us and to our children until forever, to do all [the] words of the law the this.

en.L: The hidden [things belong] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, but the revealed [things belong] to us and to our children forever, to do all the words of this law.
en.B: The hidden things belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, but what has been revealed belongs to us and to our children for all time, so that we may do all the words of this law.
en.R: Some things are hidden, and only {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God knows them. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has shown us other things, and they belong to us and to our children forever. He has shown them to us so that we may obey all the words of this teaching.

es.L: Las cosas ocultas [pertenecen] {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} nuestro Dios, pero las reveladas [nos pertenecen] a nosotros y a nuestros hijos para siempre, para que cumplamos todas las palabras de esta ley.
es.B: Lo oculto pertenece {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} nuestro Dios, pero lo revelado nos pertenece a nosotros y a nuestros hijos para siempre, para que pongamos en práctica todas las palabras de esta ley.
es.R: Hay cosas ocultas que solo conoce {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios. Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos ha mostrado otras cosas, y esas son nuestras y de nuestros hijos para siempre. Nos las ha mostrado para que obedezcamos todas las palabras de esta enseñanza.

fr.L: Les choses cachées [sont] {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} notre Dieu, mais les choses révélées [sont] à nous et à nos enfants pour toujours, afin que nous pratiquions toutes les paroles de cette loi.
fr.B: Les choses cachées appartiennent {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} notre Dieu, mais ce qui a été révélé nous appartient, à nous et à nos enfants, pour toujours, afin que nous mettions en pratique toutes les paroles de cette loi.
fr.R: Certaines choses sont cachées, et seul {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu les connaît. Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a montré d’autres choses, et elles sont à nous et à nos enfants pour toujours. C’est pour que nous obéissions à toutes les paroles de cet enseignement qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous les a montrées.

sw.B: Mambo yaliyofichika ni mali ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu, lakini yale yaliyofunuliwa ni yetu na ya watoto wetu hata milele, ili tuyatekeleze maneno yote ya sheria hii.
sw.R: Mambo mengine yamefichika, na ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu peke yake anayeyajua. Lakini ametuonyesha mambo mengine, nayo ni yetu na ya watoto wetu milele. Ametuonyesha ili tuyatii maneno yote ya mafundisho haya.

decisions.choice: the hidden things and the revealed things
decisions.reason: The verse closes the warnings with a contrast. What God has not made known, the future and his own purposes, is his alone. What he has revealed, the law Moses has taught, is given to Israel and every later generation, and it is given to be done. The verse turns the people from questions they cannot answer to the commands they can obey (30:11-14).

decisions.choice: the hidden things: possibly also hidden sins
alternatives: secret sins, which only God can punish
decisions.reason: Coming after verses 17-18, which speak of a man who turns from God in his heart where no one sees, "the hidden things" may include secret sins, which God alone can judge, while open sins are for the community to deal with. The verse does not say this outright, and the wider sense, everything God has not revealed, fits it as well.

decisions.choice: to us and to our children: written with dots over the letters
alternatives: the dots mark words to be read with special attention
the dots mark words the scribes questioned
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew text dots are written above the words "to us and to our children" and the first letter of "forever". This is one of ten places in the Torah where the scribes marked letters with such dots (another is Genesis 33:4). The dots are very old, and their purpose is not known for certain; they may mark words the scribes doubted, or draw attention to them. Ancient Jewish discussion took them here to mean that Israel was not held responsible for hidden sins until it had crossed the Jordan and made the covenant at Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim (27:1-26; Joshua 8:30-35). The words themselves are not in doubt.

decisions.choice: to do: the purpose of what God has revealed
decisions.reason: The final words say what the revealed things are for: so that Israel may do all the words of this law. Knowing is for doing (verse 8; 30:14).

decisions.choice: Some things are hidden ... But he has shown us other things
decisions.reason: Readable says the two parts of the verse as sentences with God as the one who knows and reveals, which the Hebrew implies but does not state. It says "teaching" for "law", as Deuteronomy does at Readable.

decisions.choice: no closing quotation mark
decisions.reason: Moses' speech, which began in verse 1, continues through chapter 30 and closes at 30:20, so no closing quotation mark is written at the end of this chapter.
